reference_disclaimer: These are mockups, not screenshots. Nothing shown is implemented, composed, or reachable from the running application: no widget, projection, or fetch was changed to produce them. Each one is generated from checked-in SVG by render_mockups.py, and every colour, row shape, label format and field name in it was read from live source and is cited on the subject. The conversations themselves are invented, because no recorded pull request in this repository carries a conversation at all - the deepest real structure anywhere is a single replyTo edge in a contract fixture. The first image in every comparison is the same baseline: the drawer exactly as it ships today.

subjects.description: Every thread across every file in one surface, grouped by file, plus the pull-request-level reviews and comments that the file-anchored drawer never shows at all. Choose this if the case you hit is 'I have lost track of what is still open across this review', rather than 'this one thread is too tangled to follow'. It reads the projection exactly as it is today: the only change is dropping the current-file filter and grouping by Path, so no model change and no fetch change is implied. Its real cost is a second surface that has to stay consistent with the drawer, and a second place a reviewer can lose their position.

audit_verdict.note: The reply edge this depends on was verified to exist upstream at github_read_model.hpp:233 and to be discarded at github_projection_mapping.cpp:175. The absence of any deep recorded conversation was verified against both PR recordings and the contract fixtures, and is recorded as a concern rather than an audit failure because it bears on the decision, not on whether the mockup is honest.

subjects.description: A map of one thread's reply structure, with the path from the root to where you are highlighted and one reply in focus. This is the alternative your own reference points at: Treeverse, which you reach for on Twitter threads because a linear presentation gets confusing at depth. Choose this if the case you hit is 'this one conversation is too tangled to follow inline'. Two things you should weigh before choosing it. First, the reply edge it needs is already fetched: the read model carries ReplyTo per comment and the GraphQL contract validates it, but the projection throws it away and writes the thread root as every comment's parent, so today's tree is two levels deep by construction and this view would need that one line changed. Second, and more seriously, nothing in this repository could exercise it - the conversation drawn here is invented.

detail_sections.heading: What this would cost
items: One projection line: github_projection_mapping.cpp:175 currently writes .ParentId = threadId where comment.ReplyTo is already in scope.
A new map surface plus its focus pane, keyboard navigation, and accessibility.
A recorded conversation with real depth, which does not exist yet and cannot be manufactured honestly.

audit_verdict.note: The absence of any revision identity on github_conversation_projection was verified field by field at github_projection.hpp:124-139, and the epoch label format drawn was read from epoch_history_model.cpp:132-137. The mockup asserts the gap rather than papering over it.

subjects.description: A separate question from the one above, so it is a separate decision rather than a third alternative. This is the thing you said GitHub is extra terrible at: seeing conversations and code evolve together as a PR gets new revisions. The mockup shows what it would look like if a comment knew which revision it was written against - which comments were live on each side of a comparison, and what went outdated in between. Accept means it is worth writing the RFC that this needs. Reject means not now, and the card stays recorded rather than started. Be aware of what the mockup is: the epoch axis is real and the conversation axis is real, but the join between them is not. github_conversation_projection carries no commit OID, no epoch, and no ordinal, so every cell in that grid is a value the product cannot compute today. Outdated is a boolean GitHub handed us with nothing behind it.

items.definition: accepted_pull_request_revision carries Base and Head OIDs and an Origin of live or explicit_historical_import; epoch_comparison_control already offers independent left and right selectors over retained epochs
github_conversation_projection carries Path, Line, Resolved and Outdated for every node
No commit OID, no epoch, no ordinal anywhere on the projection record
items.term: A comment's revision - does not exist

detail_sections.heading: Why this is not a slice
items: It changes what a conversation is in the model, which is RFC-BPR-0002's territory.
It consumes the epoch axis, which is RFC-BPR-0003's.
It implies a fetch that records the revision a comment was made against, whose availability has not been checked.

subjects.display_name: Conversation and code on the same revision axis - worth an RFC?
known_concerns: Whether GitHub exposes the revision a comment was made against, unauthenticated or at all, has not been checked - if it does not, the datum has to be inferred and the whole feature weakens
This crosses RFC-BPR-0002's conversation model and RFC-BPR-0003's epoch axis, so two owners have to agree before a field is added
The card explicitly warns against adding a revision field to the projection as a side effect of a presentation card, which is the cheap path this must not take
